The '''2022–23 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team''' represented [[New Mexico State University]] in the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Aggies were led by first-year head coach [[Greg Heiar]] and played their home games at the [[Pan American Center]] in [[Las Cruces, New Mexico]] as members of the [[Western Athletic Conference]]. They finished the season 9–15, 2–16 in [[Western Athletic Conference]] play to finish in last place. On February 10, 2023, the school announced the men's basketball program's season would be cancelled based on new reports of violations of university policies. The rest of the team's games were canceled and were deemed forfeits by the WAC. The NCAA does not recognize the forfeited games as part of the team's overall record. They did not take part in the [[2023 WAC men's basketball tournament|WAC Tournament]].<ref name="Forfeit2">{{cite press release |title=Remaining New Mexico State 2022–23 WAC Men’s Basketball Games Deemed Conference Forfeits |date=February 13, 2023 |publisher=Western Athletic Conference |url=https://www.wacsports.com/sports/mbkb/2022-23/Releases/nmsumbbresolution |access-date=February 14, 2023}}</ref>

On November 19, 2022, there were reports of a shooting between a student attending the [[University of New Mexico]] and a New Mexico State basketball player, leaving the student dead. The basketball player was later identified as Mike Peake, who was wounded on the UNM main campus in Albuquerque.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Grammer |first1=Geoff |last2=Reisen |first2=Matthew |date=November 19, 2022 |title=UNM Student Killed, NMSU Basketball Player Injured in Shootout on UNM Campus |url=https://www.abqjournal.com/2551440/police-investigate-homicide-on-unm-campus.html |website=Albuquerque Journal}}</ref> A day later, on November 20, 2022, the [[New Mexico State Police]] released details of the shooting, including the arrest of 17-year old Mya Hill. The next day, the New Mexico State Police confirmed a second arrest relating to the shooting, arresting 19-year old Jonathan Smith.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Peerman |first1=Lucas |last2=Groves |first2=Jason |date=November 21, 2022 |title=Details Emerge: Police Identify UNM Student Killed in Shootout with NMSU Basketball Player |url=https://www.lcsun-news.com/story/news/2022/11/21/unm-student-killed-in-shootout-with-nmsu-basketball-player-identified/69665830007 |website=Las Cruces Sun-News |location=Las Cruces, New Mexico}}</ref>

The Aggies and Lobos were slated to renew the [[Rio Grande Rivalry]] on the night of the shooting, but the game was postponed. Three days later, both schools decided to cancel the Rio Grande Rivalry for the season due to safety concerns.<ref>{{cite web |last=Schacht |first=Spencer |date=November 22, 2022 |title=UNM-NMSU Men's Basketball Games Canceled Following Shooting |url=https://www.kob.com/new-mexico/nunez-announces-unm-nmsu-will-not-play-each-other-this-season |website=[[KOB-TV|KOB]] |location=Albuquerque, New Mexico}}</ref> On December 5, NM State Athletic Director [[Mario Moccia]] announced the indefinite suspension of the 21-year old Mike Peake.<ref>{{cite web |last=Groves |first=Jason |date=December 5, 2022 |title=New Mexico State Basketball Player Mike Peake Suspended Indefinitely |url=https://www.lcsun-news.com/story/sports/2022/12/05/new-mexico-state-basketball-player-mike-peake-suspended-indefinitely/69703169007 |website=Las Cruces Sun-News |location=Las Cruces, New Mexico}}</ref> No charges have been filed against Peake in what was called a "self-defense situation",<ref>{{cite web |last=Medcalg |first=Myron |date=November 19, 2022 |title=New Mexico State-New Mexico Basketball Game Postponed after Shooting |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35060858/new-mexico-state-new-mexico-basketball-game-postponed-shooting |website=ESPN}}</ref> but there are two investigations surrounding the shooting.<ref>{{cite web |last=Boetel |first=Ryan |date=December 6, 2022 |title=DA's Office Investigating NMSU Staff and Players |url=https://www.abqjournal.com/2555661/nmsu-to-hire-outside-firm-to-probe-shooting-involving-basketball-player.html |website=Albuquerque Journal}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=NMSU Hiring 3rd Party to Investigate Events Surrounding Deadly UNM Shooting |url=https://kfoxtv.com/news/local/new-mexico-state-university-hiring-third-party-to-investigate-events-surrounding-deadly-university-of-new-mexico-shooting-police-albuquerque-mike-peake-brandon-travis-december-6-2022 |website=[[KFOX-TV]] |agency=Associated Press |location=El Paso, Texas}}</ref>

On February 10, New Mexico State University announced the men's basketball program's season would be cancelled based on new reports of violations of university policies.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hill |first=Glynn A. |date=February 11, 2023 |title=New Mexico State Men's Basketball Season Suspended, Staff Put on Leave |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/us/new-mexico-state-men-s-basketball-season-suspended-staff-put-on-leave |website=The Washington Post}}</ref> Its entire coaching staff was placed on administrative leave as a result.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 11, 2023 |title=NMSU men's hoops halted amid 'new allegations' |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35633413/nmsu-men-hoops-season-halted-indefinitely-amid-new-allegations |access-date=February 11, 2023 |work=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> [[KTSM-TV|KTSM]] reported that the season was suspended because of allegations of hazing by at least three different players multiple times.<ref>{{cite web |last=Deaver |first=Colin |date=February 10, 2023 |title=New Mexico State Men's Basketball Shuts Down Program Indefinitely; Sources Cite Hazing Incidents |url=https://www.ktsm.com/sports/college-sports/nmsu/new-mexico-state-mens-basketball-shuts-down-program-indefinitely |website=[[KTSM-TV|KTSM]] |location=El Paso, Texas}}</ref>

On February 14, head coach [[Greg Heiar]] was officially fired by NMSU.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Groves |first=Jason |date=February 14, 2023 |title=Greg Heiar fired as NMSU Aggies basketball coach amid athlete hazing investigation |url=https://www.lcsun-news.com/story/sports/college/nmsu/2023/02/14/greg-heiar-fired-as-nmsu-aggies-basketball-coach-amid-athlete-hazing-investigation/69896640007/ |access-date=February 14, 2023 |newspaper=[[Las Cruces Sun-News]]}}</ref> On March 24, the school named [[Sam Houston Bearkats baseball|Sam Houston]] head coach Jason Hooten the team's new head coach.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-25 |title=Sam Houston's Hooten to coach New Mexico St. |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35938979/new-mexico-st-hires-sam-houston-jason-hooten-next-head-coach |access-date=2023-04-04 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

The season marked the school's last in the Western Athletic Conference. The school joined Conference USA in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-01 |title=New Mexico State officially joins Conference USA ahead of 2023-24 season |url=https://www.ktsm.com/news/new-mexico-state-officially-joins-conference-usa-ahead-of-2023-24-season/ |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=KTSM 9 News |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2021–22 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team|Aggies]] finished the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]] 27–7, 14–4 in [[2021–22 Western Athletic Conference men's basketball season|WAC play]] to finish in a three-way tie for the regular season championship with [[2021–22 Seattle Redhawks men's basketball team|Seattle]] and [[2021–22 Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks basketball team|Stephen F. Austin]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wacsports.com/sports/mbkb/2021-22/standings|title=2021-22 WAC Men's Basketball Standings|work=Western Athletic Conference|access-date=January 6, 2023|language=en}}</ref> As the No. 1 seed in the  [[2022 WAC men's basketball tournament|WAC tournament]], they defeated [[2021–22 Grand Canyon Antelopes men's basketball team|Grand Canyon]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://gculopes.com/news/2022/3/11/mens-basketball-grand-canyon-new-mexico-state-wac-tournament-semifinal-recap.aspx|title=Aggies end Lopes' WAC tourney repeat bid|work=Grand Canyon University Athletics|access-date=January 6, 2023|language=en}}</ref> and [[2021–22 Abilene Christian Wildcats men's basketball team|Abilene Christian]] to win the tournament championship. As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 12 seed in the West region.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://nmstatesports.com/news/2022/3/12/mens-basketball-back-to-the-big-dance-nm-state-handles-acu-66-52-in-wac-tournament-title-clash.aspx|title=Back to the Big Dance: NM State Handles ACU, 66-52, in WAC Tournament Title Clash|work=New Mexico State University Athletics|access-date=January 6, 2023|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ktsm.com/sports/college-sports/nmsu/new-mexico-state-earns-12-seed-in-ncaa-tournament-will-face-5-seed-uconn-thursday-in-buffalo-n-y/|title=New Mexico State earns 12-seed in NCAA Tournament, will face 5-seed UConn Thursday in Buffalo, N.Y.|work=KTSM 9 News|access-date=January 6, 2023|language=en}}</ref> There they upset No. 5-seeded [[2021–22 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]] in the First Round<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2022/03/17/new-mexico-state-12-seed-stuns-5-uconn/7084641001/|title=No. 12 seed New Mexico State shocks No. 5 UConn in NCAA Tournament bracket-buster|work=[[USA Today]]|access-date=January 6, 2023|language=en}}</ref> before losing to No. 4-seeded [[2021–22 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]] in the Second Round.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.swtimes.com/story/sports/college/2022/03/19/arkansas-advances-sweet-16-close-win-over-new-mexico-state-ncaa-tournament/7049014001/|title=Arkansas survives scare from New Mexico State, advances to NCAA Tournament Sweet 16|work=Fort Smith Times Record|access-date=January 6, 2023|language=en}}</ref>
